name: hollow_section_ac
description: Section-Mapped Process Hollowing against a fresh AssaultCube 1.3.0.2 instance. Attacker launches a NEW ac_client.exe CREATE_SUSPENDED (never actually starts the game's main loop), maps a shared RWX section into both attacker and victim address spaces, writes a 10-byte shellcode locally, and redirects the victim's initial thread to that shellcode via SetThreadContext. The shellcode fires (counter observed via attacker's own view of the shared physical pages), then the victim AC instance is terminated before it ever renders a frame. This validates that (a) the classifier's new MAPVIEW rule fires against real AC binaries, (b) the technique works against 32-bit victims (AC is x86), and (c) our attacker (32-bit ProcessToolkit) can hollow another 32-bit process. Note: AC's own --home / config args are NOT passed because AC's main loop never runs — the shellcode replaces the entry point before RtlUserThreadStart transfers control to AC's crt0. This is a valid demonstration of the ATTACK, not a demonstration of running AC in a modified form.

extra.runner_target_note: The runner-launched target (TestTarget) is unrelated to the attack — it exists only because the runner's manifest schema requires a target. The ATTACK's victim is a fresh AC process spawned by the attacker (ProcessToolkit) via CreateProcess(CREATE_SUSPENDED). Classifier verdicts scoped to the runner target may miss the interesting cross-process events (which target the victim PID, not the runner target PID). See rule_classifier.py's design note on attacker-scoped vs target-scoped detection.
extra.expected_fingerprint: 1x MAPVIEW_REMOTE (attacker → victim AC), 1x SETTHREADCONTEXT_REMOTE (RIP redirect to shellcode entry in victim's view), 1x CreateProcess KernelProcess event (spawned ac_client.exe). Notably absent: ALLOCVM_REMOTE, WRITEVM_REMOTE (section delivery replaces them), THREAD_CREATE_REMOTE (victim's own initial thread runs the shellcode).
